record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: Let G^1_ψ(M) denote either the C¹ smooth-measure-preserving or the C¹ symplectic diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M, and let SE^1_ψ be the class of maps that remain uniformly positive in maximal Lyapunov exponent on all nearby periodic-orbit measures under small C¹ perturbations. Is the subset of maps in G^1_ψ(M) that admit a dominated splitting on all of M C¹-dense inside SE^1_ψ?

evidence.quote: Is the set {f ∈ G1ψ(M); f has a dominated splitting on M} C1-dense in SE1ψ ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold (possibly equipped with a smooth volume form, or with a symplectic form when applicable). Let $G^1_\psi(M)$ denote either:
(i) the space of $C^1$ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, or
(ii) the space of $C^1$ symplectic diffeomorphisms of $M$ (when $M$ carries a symplectic structure),
endowed with the $C^1$ topology.

For $f \in G^1_\psi(M)$ and a periodic point $p$ of $f$ with period $\pi(p)$, let $\lambda^+(f,p)$ denote the largest Lyapunov exponent of the linear map $Df^{\pi(p)}(p)$, i.e. the maximal exponential growth rate of $\|Df^n\|$ along the orbit of $p$. Say that $f$ has uniformly positive maximal periodic exponent if there exists $c(f) > 0$ such that $\lambda^+(f,p) \ge c(f)$ for every periodic point $p$ of $f$. Define
$$SE^1_\psi = \{ f \in G^1_\psi(M) : \text{there exist a } C^1\text{-neighborhood } \mathcal{U} \text{ of } f \text{ and } c > 0 \text{ with } \lambda^+(g,p) \ge c \text{ for every } g \in \mathcal{U} \text{ and every periodic point } p \text{ of } g \}.$$

Recall that $f$ admits a dominated splitting on $M$ if the tangent bundle $TM$ decomposes as a continuous $Df$-invariant Whitney sum $TM = E \oplus F$ with $E,F$ nontrivial such that there exist constants $C>0$ and $0<\lambda<1$ with
$$\|Df^n|_{E(x)}\| \cdot \|Df^{-n}|_{F(f^n(x))}\| \le C\lambda^n \quad \text{for all } x\in M, n\ge 0.$$

Question: Is the set
$$\{ f \in G^1_\psi(M) : f \text{ admits a dominated splitting on all of } M \}$$
$C^1$-dense in $SE^1_\psi$?
artifact.status_search_result: Related results by Bochi, Viana, Avila–Crovisier–Wilkinson, and others establish dichotomies between dominated splitting and vanishing Lyapunov exponents for C¹-generic conservative/symplectic diffeomorphisms, and link continuity of Lyapunov exponents to domination. However, no source directly confirms or refutes the precise C¹-density statement of the dominated-splitting set inside the class of stably uniformly positive maximal periodic exponents. The problem appears to remain open as of the available literature.

status_evidence.title: The Lyapunov exponents of generic volume-preserving and symplectic maps (Bochi–Viana)
status_evidence.snippet: Continuity of integrated Lyapunov exponents at f forces either trivial Oseledets splitting or dominated splitting a.e.
status_evidence.claim: Related dichotomy theorem; does not resolve the C¹-density question for SE¹_ψ.

status_evidence.title: C¹ density of stable ergodicity (Avila–Crovisier–Wilkinson)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies C¹-generic conservative diffeomorphisms with partial hyperbolicity / dominated structures.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related framework but does not establish the precise density claim.

status_evidence.title: C¹-generic symplectic diffeomorphisms: partial hyperbolicity and zero centre Lyapunov exponents
status_evidence.snippet: For a residual set of C¹ symplectic diffeomorphisms, either Anosov or zero Lyapunov exponent of multiplicity ≥ 2 a.e.
status_evidence.claim: Provides generic dichotomy supporting context, not a resolution.
